title: The Condon band of 1951: packed house and Chicago style
summary: Leeman joined in 1951 with Wild Bill Davison, Edmund Hall, Cutty Cutshall, Gene Schroeder and others, playing straight-down-the-middle jazz and requested traditional songs to jammed rooms.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: To get back to the Condon band, when I went in with Eddie in '51, that band was the most charging band, the most exciting -- I don't believe they ever had a bad night. I can't remember a bad night there. That was with Wild Bill -- Wild Bill Davison, Edmund Hall, Cutty Cutshall, Schroeder Gene Shrader -- Shrader Shroder -- take your pick.

I got Walter Page, I recommended Walter Page for the job, and Ralph Sutton, Lou McGerrity, and -- in those days, the place was jammed. I've seen them hang from the -- there was a railing around the top there, there was an upper part, and they'd come down from West Point, the Army-Navy games and so forth. And we played with that band, all the traditional Dixieland songs, because they were requested. They were references -- it was a Dixie style orchestra, which it was not. With Wild Bill and Eddie, and the manner in which we played could be referred to as the Chicago jazz style, it was just straight jazz down the middle.
